about: Shared by backend/tests/test_model_pricing.py and frontend/tests/lib/pricing.test.ts so the two estimators agree. A case's optional `wired` lists input ports with an edge into them. The `table` node is a five-route table (services/node_route.py routes): its price entry keys each route by its `pricing` or id, `runCases` price a whole run (estimate_run / summarizeRunScope) with the keys in `apiKeys`, and `routeEstimateCases` give each route's price (estimate_routes / estimateRoutes). A route entry with `unconfirmed: true` is a price the provider's page doesn't state exactly (the switcher marks it with *; route_price_unconfirmed / routePriceUnconfirmed). The `moded` node prices by `(mode)`, a price variable read from the wired ports (v2v with start_video, i2v with start_image, keyframes or end_image, else t2v; model_pricing.VIDEO_MODE / pricing.ts VIDEO_MODE), and `tooled` by run-time quantities of its source clip ((source seconds), (output megapixels): RUN_TIME_VARIABLES), so it is unpriced before the run. `shippedRouteCases` price the registry's route-table nodes with the shipped table (backend/data/model_pricing.json): each route's price as a number, a [low, high] range, or null, and optionally `unconfirmed`: whether each route's price is marked at those params (route_price_unconfirmed / routePriceUnconfirmed; a row may carry its own `unconfirmed`, as FLUX.2's Flash and Klein rows on fal do). `shippedRunCases` price a whole run of a registry node on the shipped table (estimate_run / summarizeRunScope) with the keys in `apiKeys` and the ports in `wired` (one edge each). Krea 3 also prices by `(references)`, read from the wired ports: `some` with an edge into `images`, else `none` (model_pricing.REFERENCES / pricing.ts REFERENCES). The `tiered` node prices by `(wired refs)`, read from the wired ports: `yes` with an edge into `refs`, else `no` (model_pricing.WIRED_PREFIX / pricing.ts WIRED_PREFIX); every row that reads the `refs` param also reads `(wired refs)`, so a wire into `refs` is priced, not unknown, while the `loose` node's row reads `refs` alone and stays unpriced with it wired. Krea 2 prices by k2BillingTier this way (shippedRunCases), and its entries list the params the handler strips in `whitespaceUnset`, so a whitespace-only value there prices as unset (only those params: `tiered` counts a whitespace `refs` as set). A case's optional `size` is the measured input of the port its entry's `sizing` names ({width, height, seconds, frames}: model_pricing.estimate_node size / pricing.ts estimateNode size): the `sized` node prices per megapixel of the larger of input and output, rounded up, and `tooled` per megapixel-second of output; without a size both are unpriced. `sizedRunCases` price a whole run of a registry node on the shipped table with its sizing port wired from an Image Input or Video Input whose file measured `size` (estimate_run sizes / summarizeRunScope sizes); `awaitingInput` is whether the node is unpriced only because its input's size isn't known. Every run case's `expected.reason` is why the node leaves the total open, or null (estimate_run `reasons` / summarizeRunScope `reasons`): {kind: noPrice | cantRun | awaitingInput | missingKey with the `keys` it needs | leftOut with its `plus` | plan for a run on the Krea plan}; the proposal bar's Accept chip writes its reason lines from it. `classCases` run several nodes together (the fixture's definitions over the registry's, the fixture's prices over the shipped table's) and give each node's cost class (model_pricing.cost_class / costClass): `paid`, `plan` (the Krea plan), `free` (a key-billing route with no key, or a sourced $0 such as the `zeroed` node's) and `mayCost`, with the paid figure (`low`/`high`, null when no paid node is priced) and whether the run is a sourced $0 (`sourcedZero`): estimate_run `classes` / summarizeRunScope `paid`, `plan`, `free`, `mayCost`.

sizing.say: $0.001 per megapixel of the larger of input and output, rounded up to a whole megapixel
